Speechify’s text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App.&nbsp;Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its 2025 Design Award winner for Inclusivity.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p>Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Overview</strong></p> <p style="text-align: left;" data-speechify-sentence="">The Platform team owns the backend behind everything Speechify ships: the public TTS API,&nbsp;payments, subscriptions, auth, consumption tracking, and analytics — serving over 50&nbsp;million users across iOS, Android, Mac, Chrome, and web.</p> <p style="text-align: left;" data-speechify-sentence="">These are systems where correctness compounds. Subscription state has to stay consistent&nbsp;across five clients and two app-store billing systems that each go quiet at the worst moment.&nbsp;Consumption metering has to be exact enough to bill on and cheap enough to run at our&nbsp;request volume. The public TTS API has external customers with their own products&nbsp;depending on our latency and uptime. You'll work closely with our Sales team to prospect and nurture relationships with CFO, CPO, CEO and CIO stakeholders, and drive sales opportunities for our Agentic AI platform automating Purchase-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash. You will have a proactive approach and work to accelerate the sales process, convert leads into qualified opportunities, and consistently hit sales targets. Craft tailored value propositions by understanding the unique pain points of stakeholders across Finance, Procurement, and IT in Purchase-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash processes. Prospect large accounts and build multi-threaded stakeholder maps across Finance, Procurement, IT and the executive sponsor. Run and present in 30-minute discovery calls with C-level stakeholders. You own the meeting, not just the booking. Stay ahead of the market by continuously updating your commercial knowledge, analysing procurement and finance processes, and tracking industry trends in Agentic AI and ERP automation. Prioritise complex tasks with clients, flagging bottlenecks early rather than late to keep things moving forward. Carry a quota of 1.2M ARR closed-won sourced per year. We're excited about you because You have 2-4 years of experience in a B2B SaaS sales environment, ideally selling into manufacturing, industrial or finance/procurement buyers, and a track record of building stakeholder maps in commercial accounts while consistently exceeding sales targets. You communicate clearly, concisely, and persuasively, with the ability to adapt your style to a CFO, CPO, CEO or CIO conversation. You handle rejection with resilience and keep your momentum through long, multi-stakeholder commercial sales cycles. You're a team player with a sense of ownership and accountability. You enjoy problem-solving and have a natural curiosity that drives you to find creative solutions. Bonus Points: You have experience selling into Manufacturing, Industrial or Finance/procurement buyers, are familiar with ERP systems or sales tech

title: Marketing Manager - Manda
description: The company It's still difficult for business owners to sell their business, or buy others, in the sub-£10m enterprise value market. Information asymmetry, lack of knowledge and low transaction values make it hard, and most M&A firms shy away from the segment because they can't serve it profitably. A generation of owner-managers is approaching retirement, and most of them have no realistic route to a sale. manda exists to fix that. We match buyers with sellers in the part of the market everyone else ignores, and we finance acquisitions ourselves so buyers arrive pre-qualified and often pre-financed. We've sold the first businesses, funded the first acquisition loans, and we're now opening the platform up beyond the businesses that already bank with us. manda is part of iwoca, one of Europe's leading fintech lenders. Since 2012 iwoca has provided more than £4 billion in funding and its mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments. That backing is why we can serve this market where others can't: a deep footprint in the SME economy with 150,000+ UK customers, the data and infrastructure of an established lender, and the ability to build clean, automated processes instead of running an advisory firm on spreadsheets. We're looking for a Marketing Manager to own how business owners find manda, iwoca's M&A platform. You'll be our first marketing hire, joining as we open the platform to business owners who don't yet bank with iwoca. Almost everything about how we reach them is still to be decided, and you'll be the one deciding it. The team You'll be our first marketing hire, joining a founding team of circa 10 mandans. All highly motivated to finally free the SME M&A space from the lack of meaningful innovation in the space. You'll get the autonomy and pace of a startup, with the data, infrastructure and credibility of an established lender behind you. You'll report directly into the Venture Lead of manda. Your mission Your mission is to bring the right business owners to manda: people genuinely thinking about selling, at the point in their lives when they're thinking about it. Today almost all of our sellers come from iwoca's own customer base, found by hand and worked one at a time. That works, but it doesn't scale and the pool is finite. Your job is to build the channels that reach owners who have never heard of iwoca, work out which of those channels produce real mandates at a cost our fee model can support, and shut down the ones that don't. You won't be inheriting a growth engine. We're launching our direct application journey this autumn, and filling it is your first job. You'll be building the first growth engine here, and you'll be the person who decides where the money goes. The role Find the channels that work Run cheap, fast tests across direct channels such as paid search, paid social, organic, and direct response. Prioritise those that work and kill the ones that don't, based on evidence. Own the budget and the allocation decisions. You'll start small on purpose: we'd rather learn which channel works than spend heavily on one that doesn't. Write and test the copy yourself, from ads to landing pages, and iterate on what real business owners actually respond to. Test offline as well as digital. Mail and email direct to business owners are two of the few ways to reach someone who isn't actively searching for a way out, and nobody has tested either properly for us yet.
